title: Listening & Reading
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata dan struktur untuk memperkenalkan diri serta menanyakan informasi kepada orang lain.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 11-13
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to understand and identify additional key vocabulary from this page.
Learners will be able to understand people talking about where they live.
Learners will be able to understand and identify additional key vocabulary from this page.
Learners will be able to understand a text about someone giving personal information.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feeling. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 11.
Tell them that they need to listen and number the pictures in the order they hear them according to the audio.

Before listening, practice pronunciation of the words in task A. The teacher says the two vocabulary choices given for each number. For example, ‘an apartment, close to, etc.’. Ask students to repeat the words aloud and continue for all words.
Play audio 1.3. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check students’ understanding.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner and then check the answers together.

Play audio again and ask students to write down the sentences they hear in their notebooks (this is a simple dictation activity). Then show the audio script and ask students to correct their sentences.
Or show the audio script on the screen, and ask students to read the sentences aloud together.
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the words they hear.
Play audio 1.4 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
In order to make vocabulary drilling more interesting, students could be guided to drill using different emotions (e.g. excited or surprised) or voices.
Students are going to complete task C. Allow them to read the task and look at the pictures before they listen and circle the correct answer.
Play audio 1.5. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students to choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures on Student Book page 12-13.
Ask some specific questions about the pictures, for example, ‘How many people can you see?’, ‘Where are they?’

Giving some personal questions is also suggested to make it more relatable to students, for example, “How do you feel at the first day of school?” or “Do you think it is easy or difficult to make new friends?”
Tell students they are going to listen to the audio and point to the pictures.
Before playing audio 1.6, say the new vocabulary and ask students to repeat after you for pronunciation practice or you can play the audio again and ask students to repeat the key vocabulary.
Ask students to look at task B on Student Book page 12.
Put students in pairs and ask them to answer the questions together. Tell students they only need to write one or two words, and that the answers will be the vocabulary from Reading A.
Give students 3-4 minutes to complete the task.
Elicit answers from students. Write the answers on the board.
Tell them to practice asking and correctly answering the questions together.
First, Student A asks the questions and Student B answers them. Then switch the role.
Tell students that they will listen and read the story. Play audio 1.7 and ask them to read the text silently.
Next, play the audio again and ask students to read the text aloud, following the audio. Ask if there are any questions about the language in the text.
Now, students read the yes/no statements together as a class and they need to circle 'yes' or 'no' about each statement according to the information given in the text.
The first question can be done together as a class to make sure students know what to do.
Then, they can complete the task in pairs or by themselves.
Ask students to check their answers with a friend.
Check the answers as a class. Write the answers on the board.
To make the checking answer stage more fun and encourage participation from the whole class, each student could show their answer by showing an object with certain colour.
For example, if they think the answer is yes, show something blue. If they think the answer is no, show something red.
Now ask students to look at task E on page 13.
Read the questions aloud together as a class.
Tell students to write answers to the questions about themselves.
Give students 4-5 minutes to write their answers.
Put students in pairs.
This activity could be done if there is more time.
Put the students into groups of 3. Ask them to choose a character in the script and practice reading it aloud together.
After students practice the conversation the first time, play audio 1.7 again and ask students to pay attention to the pronunciation and intonation.
Then, tell students to switch roles so they can practice speaking as another character.
Ask students to re-write the conversation, but change the names and other personal information (address, birthday, if they live close to or far from school, etc.) to be about themselves.
Give students around 7-8 minutes to write their new conversation in their notebooks.
Tell students that every member of the group should have the conversation written in their notebooks, not just one group member.
Tell students to practice their new conversation and ask them to perform their conversations in front of the class.
Teachers can give simple questions to check what students have learned, for example, “How do you ask the question if you want to know my age?”
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: ketepatan jawaban tugas listening (menomori/menjodohkan/melengkapi).
Pertanyaan pemahaman bacaan (literal & inferensial) dan pembahasan bersama.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
